subject: Art & Design
title: Hierarchy: Guiding the Reader's Eye
description: A quick, practical guide to Hierarchy: Guiding the Reader's Eye.

hook.text: Your eye just skipped to the biggest text on this screen. That's typographic hierarchy doing its job.

buildup.text: Hierarchy uses size, weight, color, and spacing to signal what's most important and what's supporting.

discovery.text: Three levels usually suffice: headline (attention), subhead (context), and body (detail).

twist.text: If everything is bold, nothing is bold. Hierarchy only works when some elements are deliberately quiet.

climax.text: Squint at your design. If you can still tell what's most important, your hierarchy works.

punchline.text: Hierarchy doesn't shout louder. It whispers quieter everywhere else.

quiz.question: How do you test if your typographic hierarchy works?
options: Squint — if you can still tell what's important, it works
Use the largest font size everywhere

details.summary: Typographic hierarchy uses size, weight, color, and spacing to create a clear order of importance — headlines, subheadings, body text, captions. This visual structure guides readers through content in an intentional sequence, telling them what to read first, second.
details.whyItMatters: Without hierarchy, all text competes equally for attention and nothing feels important. Clear typographic hierarchy is the single most important factor in making content scannable, navigable, and comprehensible.
takeaways: Hierarchy uses size, weight, and color for importance ordering
It guides readers through content in an intentional sequence
Clear hierarchy makes content scannable and comprehensible

faq.question: How many levels of hierarchy should a design have?
faq.answer: Most content needs three to four levels: title, subheadings, body text, and captions or metadata. More than five levels become hard to distinguish visually. Each level should be clearly different from adjacent levels — a subtle size change between H2 and H3 creates confusion.

faq.question: What creates the strongest hierarchy contrast?
faq.answer: Size difference is the most immediate hierarchy signal. A headline three times larger than body text creates unambiguous hierarchy. Combine with weight (bold vs. regular), color contrast, and whitespace for reinforced distinction.
